title: Fix definition of GroupNormalization
body:
# Ask a Question

### Question
According to the document of GroupNormalization's operator 
https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/main/docs/Operators.md#groupnormalization
I found the tensor shape of both scale and bias are num_groups.
However, this should be equal to C instead of G.

### Further information
- Relevant Area: operators
-According to the paper (page 4)
https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.08494.pdf
Shape of Gamma (scale) and beta (bias) ic C (perchannel not pergroup).
![image](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/assets/9115697/8622ff58-122f-4ee4-a182-9f7f14caecc3)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
According to the implementation of onnxruntime, shape of gamma and beta is also [C], 
https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/blob/HEAD/onnxruntime/contrib_ops/cuda/diffusion/group_norm.cc#L91-L98

In addition, I also check the implementation of pytorch
![image](https://github.com/onnx/onnx/assets/9115697/da237e78-2301-413d-976e-40f739c87087)

The result is also the same
gamma =  tensor([1., 1., 1., 1., 1., 1.])
beta =  tensor([0., 0., 0., 0., 0., 0.])

Hence, I thought the doc of onnx operator may be incorrect and need to be revised.

comments.author: participant2
reporter
comments.body:
> @reporter Thanks for bringing this up. It does seem like the ONNX spec is being more restrictive than the version in the paper and PyTorch. The current ONNXRuntime implementation, though, follows the ONNX spec with per-group scale and bias. What you linked to above seems to be the `com.microsoft.GroupNorm` op.
> 
> To determine next steps, I think it would be useful to look at some practical use cases first. I'm wondering if you have some concrete models where per-channel scale and bias are needed?

Stable diffusion require groupnorm operator.
You could reference follow model
https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/blob/main/onnxruntime/python/tools/transformers/models/stable_diffusion/README.md

By the way, you mention the link I provide is **com.microsoft.GroupNorm**.  I wonder is there any other groupnorm in onnxruntime is per-group scale and bias?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@reporter Thanks for the reference. Does this stable diffusion model actually use different scale and bias for each channel? Or do it use the default values of 1 and 0 respectively? I've seen resnet models where the scale and bias are always kept at the default values. But regardless, I think matching pytorch's implementaion is strong enough reason for us to extend this op in coming opsets. I'm just trying to gather more info on the impact of this limitation.

In onnxruntime, the standard implementation for `GroupNormalization` (note the name difference) uses per-group sclae and bias. You can verify this by running a simple onnx model through onnxruntime. If the scale and bias inputs have length C instead of G, then it'll complain about shape mismatch.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> GroupNormalization

stable diffusion does not use default value of gamma and beta.
In addition, traditional Resnet use batchnorm instead of groupnorm.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: I agree we should update to match what is in the paper and match pytorch, because the spec is defined based on the paper.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: This was discussed in the operator SIG meeting last week, and the op's spec will be updated.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
~Should we deprecate the old spec?~

Update: no from the discussion.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: @participant2 gentle nudge. Do you have any updates? We are targeting this for the 1.16 release.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> @participant2 gentle nudge. Do you have any updates? We are targeting this for the 1.16 release.

As I mentioned in my message to @participant1 , I wonder if we should apply an individual fix to this op or should we make this fix when unifying the normalization ops. An individual fix should be faster if we are targeting the next release.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: I vote for fixing this op first, as the error has been around for a while and it is preventing adoption of this operator.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: @participant3 May I ask what's the projected timeline for 1.16 release?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I think we should ideally target February for the next release (aiming for code-freeze by end of January or so). But this is contingent upon finding a release-manager, etc.
